messages:
jason: Heads up — customer onboarding for an EU bank wants BYOK with on-prem HSM in our Private deployment. They asked for operator separation and detailed audit logs. Quick q: what exact RBAC changes do we need for HSM proxy operators vs infra SREs?
leah: @jason +1. Segregate roles: `hsm-operator` (can import/unwrap), `hsm-auditor` (read-only logs/attest), `infra-admin` (network/config). infra-admin MUST NOT have import or key-access perms. Also recommend time-bound JIT for operator keys and approval workflow.
sam: Agree. Import and any root-key-handling actions must be logged with at minimum: actor, action, key-id, nonce, attestation-hash, requestor-tenant, syscall-context. Logs should be immutable append-only and shipped to a customer-controlled KMS-backed sink.
anya: For KMS integration, customer wants to use their AWS CloudHSM + CMK. We'll proxy but ensure plaintext key material never leaves their HSM. Use asymmetric wrapping where possible; our proxy performs `WrapKey`/`UnwrapKey` with customer public key and logs attestations. Minimal protocol sketch: ```1) Customer HSM generates ephemeral wrapping key + attestation. 2) Customer returns wrapping pubkey + attestation. 3) Our import agent wraps model key with pubkey; only wrapped blob stored. 4) Unwrap requires HSM handshake and attestation verification.```
leah: Also, for vuln triage: if a CVE affects the HSM agent we must trigger the break-glass rotation flow and notify compliance + customer. The runbook should list telemetry to capture (firmware, agent version, syscall trace), rotation steps, proof-of-rotation evidence and post-incident attestation.
security-bot: policy-diff detected: proposed role `hsm-operator` grants `kms:ImportKey` and `hsm:operatorHandshake`; manual approval required from sec-lead. See https://redwood.internal/policy-diff/6123456789 :warning:
jason: Ok — can we get a proposed RBAC patch? Sam, can you draft a minimal policy JSON snippet. Leah, can you add break-glass runbook blurb? Need by EOD for onboarding.
sam: Draft snippet (inline): ```{
  "Version":"2024-01-01",
  "Statement":[
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["hsm:ImportKey","hsm:UnwrapKey"],"Resource":"arn:redwood:hsm:eu-1:acct:tenant/*","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"hsm:Role":"hsm-operator"}}}
  ]
}``` This is minimal — will add conditions for `ipRange`, `mfa`, and `approval_ticket`.
leah: Audit event proposal: fields = event.type, actor.id, role, request_id, key_id, attestation_sig, firmware_version, agent_version, syscall_trace, tenant_id. Retention: for regulated EU customers set default 7y; ensure export-controls box checked and KMS envelope for offsite export. Also add `evidence_bucket` tagging and signed manifests for each import.
anya: Quick Q: Who owns orchestration for rotation? Product ops or customer? For Private VPC we run the orchestration but only with customer-provided attestation tokens — legal needs to sign the SLA paragraph.
sam: Ops will own orchestration but only after attestation handshake from customer HSM. We'll implement canary rotates (small subset of replicas) and fallback to read-only replica model until rotation fully converges. Also add automated verification hooks to confirm KV cache invalidation.
jason: Thanks all. Next steps: sam opens RFC PR with policy JSON + unit test harness; leah writes break-glass runbook + audit schema; anya captures SLA bullet for onboarding doc and flags legal. Ping me when each is ready. :thumbsup:
